name: MMStar
description: MMStar is an elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans. It benchmarks 6 core capabilities (Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, Mathematics) and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples that exhibit visual dependency, minimal data leakage, and require advanced multi-modal capabilities.
creator: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao (University of Science and Technology of China, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shanghai AI Laboratory)
citeAs: Chen, L., Li, J., Dong, X., Zhang, P., Zang, Y., Chen, Z., Duan, H., Wang, J., Qiao, Y., Lin, D., & Zhao, F. (2024). Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv:2403.20330.
rai:dataCollection: Samples were first roughly selected from six existing multi-modal benchmarks (SEED-Bench, AI2D, ScienceQA, MMBench, MathVista, MMMU) using an automated pipeline with LLM inspectors to filter for visual dependency and minimal data leakage, followed by strict manual review by three experts to curate 1,500 high-quality samples.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples sourced from six existing multi-modal benchmarks: SEED-Bench (SEED-Image), AI2D (AI2D-Test), ScienceQA (ScienceQA-Test), MMBench (MMBench-EN-Dev), MathVista (MathVista-Mini), and MMMU (MMMU-Val), totaling 22,401 initial samples.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Some samples were transformed from uni-modal to multi-modal formats to prevent LLMs from recalling correct answers, ensuring visual dependency.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated coarse filtering pipeline was applied using eight LLM inspectors (two closed-source: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro; six open-source: LLaMA-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B) with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy. Samples answerable by more than 2 of the 8 LLMs were excluded, reducing the pool from 22,401 to 11,607. Then 16 LVLMs were used to gauge difficulty, splitting samples into four levels: easy (12-16 hits), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3).
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted manual review to ensure: (1) each sample's answer requires understanding of visual content; (2) selected samples cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; (3) most samples require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities. Samples were split into four difficulty categories based on LVLM hit counts, and 1,500 high-quality samples were manually curated considering diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Difficulty levels were determined by tallying hit counts of 16 LVLMs on coarsely filtered samples: easy (12-16 hits), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). LLM hit rate analysis was used to validate visual dependency and minimal data leakage of the final benchmark.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Three domain experts (specific demographics not reported).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Eight LLM inspectors used for automated coarse filtering: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro (closed-source); LLaMA2-70B, Qwen-1.5-72B, Mixtral-8x7B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Deepseek-67B (open-source). Sixteen LVLMs used for difficulty assessment: GPT4V, GeminiPro-Vision, TinyLLaVA-3B, Yi-VL series, Qwen-VL-Chat, LLaVA-1.5 series, ShareGPT4V-7B, Monkey-Chat, LLaVA-Next, Deepseek-VL-7B, LLaVA-Next-34B, CogVLM-Chat-17B, InternVL-Chat-v1.2, Sphinx-X-8x7B. VLMEvalKit used as evaluation codebase.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM and LVLM training corpora.
rai:dataSocialImpact: MMStar addresses critical issues in LVLM evaluation—visual content unnecessity and unintentional data leakage—that can lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal capabilities and misguide LVLM research. By providing a fair and reliable benchmark, it aims to advance the field of multi-modal language model research and enable more accurate comparisons of LVLMs.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark is sourced predominantly from SEED-Bench (28.3% of final 1,500 samples), with other benchmarks contributing smaller proportions. The initial pool was heavily skewed toward SEED (63.5%), which may influence the distribution of capability dimensions despite efforts to balance them.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark consists of only 1,500 samples, which may limit comprehensive coverage. The coarse filtering threshold (samples answerable by more than 2 of 8 LLMs excluded) may not perfectly eliminate all data leakage or visual-unnecessary samples. The benchmark is static and may become susceptible to data leakage over time as new LLMs and LVLMs are trained on larger corpora.
rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) on multi-modal capabilities across 6 core dimensions and 18 detailed axes. The benchmark is designed to assess actual multi-modal gains and detect data leakage using the proposed Multi-modal Gain (MG) and Multi-modal Leakage (ML) metrics. Not recommended for training or fine-tuning due to its small size and the risk of contaminating the evaluation set.
